body:
CHIEF FINDING — THE SWEEP HAD A BLIND SPOT, and I found it by refusing to close a bead on two
good audits without looking.

new-engineer asked me to ACK and close bd-01M158KA75HGGM118P3SQ1RHYK as a status correction.
Two independent audits said all five identity items were already on main; m1's was
file-and-line, new-engineer's was 147/147 with four mutation kills. Both were right and I have
closed it. But m1's note flagged an interaction with 4383a85 that got truncated in display, so I
went to read the test it referred to, and the test contains this:

  val changed = fixture.recall.copy(units = ...)

recall/graph.scala:12 is `final case class RecallGraph(` -- PUBLIC constructor, public copy, no
witness. graph.scala:34 is `def validated(g: RecallGraph): ValidatedNec[DomainError, RecallGraph]`
-- it takes the type and RETURNS THE SAME TYPE. So a validated graph and an unchecked one are the
same type, and validation is advisory. Six direct constructions exist in main and none must pass
through it.

Which means m1's text-at-span law, which landed today and on which I closed two beads this
morning, is CORRECTLY IMPLEMENTED AND NOT ENFORCEABLE. Filed as
bd-01M16V1QAXR4JT1F174H2BTQT3.

NOW THE GENERAL POINT, which matters more than the one type.

The fromProduct sweep enumerated PRIVATE-CONSTRUCTOR CASE CLASSES: 84 of them, 80 with public
fromProduct, 45 guarding real validation. That population was chosen because those are the types
whose declared boundary is defeated by Mirror. It is a good population and the sweep did real
work on it -- five slices closed today.

But it can only find types that were TRYING to be boundaries and failing. RecallGraph never
tried. It has no private constructor to defeat, so it appeared in no slice's scope, and it will
never appear in any refinement of that scope. A SWEEP FOR DEFEATED BOUNDARIES CANNOT FIND A
MISSING ONE. The stricter you make the fromProduct criterion, the further RecallGraph gets from
view.

The complementary population is: types that carry an INVARIANT SOMEWHERE -- a validated(), a
check(), a law in laws/ -- but no construction boundary at all. The greppable signature is the
one RecallGraph wears: a validator whose return type is its own argument type. That signature
says, in the type system's own words, "I checked this and I have no way to tell you." Anywhere
that shape appears, the invariant is a suggestion.

I am adding this to the sweep parent bd-01M1697234KP2X44X6Q8S6C6Y7 as a second population rather
than opening a rival sweep, because it is the same defect class seen from the other side and
splitting it would lose that.

AND THE PROCESS POINT, since I have been strict with others about it today. Two competent
independent audits both said "complete, nothing owed", and both were CORRECT about the question
they were asked. Neither was wrong. The gap was in the question -- nobody had asked whether the
law being audited could be bypassed, because the bead was about identity binding, not about
construction. Agreement between independent reviewers is strong evidence about the thing
reviewed and none at all about the thing nobody thought to review.
